historical_references.title: Uniforms, ranks and identity / 制服、军衔与身份
historical_references.limitation: 原文研究记录；不等于资产采用或运行验收。 / Research notes; not asset adoption or runtime acceptance.
historical_references.excerpt:
# Uniforms, ranks and identity / 制服、军衔与身份

U.S. field jackets, M1 helmets, web equipment and dated rank plates provide appearance comparisons for the Allied soldier and first-person sleeve. The Army's uniform survey spans multiple periods: later M1943 clothing and M1944/M1945 equipment do not establish a universal August 1944 outfit. Officer and enlisted rank insignia must remain separate from divisional identity. The purchased paratrooper's exact unit and issued loadout remain unverified.

美军野战夹克、M1钢盔、携行具和有日期的军衔图用于外观比较。制服调查跨多个年代，不能把后期装备整套套用为1944年8月标准装束；军衔与师级徽记须分别核对。购买的伞兵模型所属单位与具体配发装备仍待证据确认。

The 1945 Allied handbook distinguishes German Heer uniforms, rank and branch markings. It is later than the Paris battle and is not an inventory of a particular garrison. Monochrome plates do not calibrate fabric or piping colors. British/Canadian sheets remain separate comparisons; they do not identify an American model.

1945年盟军手册可用于辨别德军陆军制服、军衔和兵种，但不能证明巴黎某守备单位的实际配装。黑白图不能作为布料或滚边颜色标定。英军、加拿大资料仅作独立比较，不代表美军角色。

Sources: U.S. Army uniform survey, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Survey_of_U.S._Army_Uniforms,_Weapons_and_Accoutrements_%282007%29,_by_David_Cole.pdf ; German handbook

note.zh: 复用制服与军衔辨别文字；原诺曼底单位和制作建议不作为巴黎角色的采用依据。
note.en: Reuse uniform and rank distinctions only; original Normandy unit assignments and production recommendations do not authorize Paris character adoption.

historical_references.title: Uniforms, ranks and identity / 制服、军衔与身份
historical_references.limitation: 原文研究记录；不等于资产采用或运行验收。 / Research notes; not asset adoption or runtime acceptance.
historical_references.excerpt:
# Uniforms, ranks and identity / 制服、军衔与身份

U.S. field jackets, M1 helmets, web equipment and dated rank plates provide appearance comparisons for the Allied soldier and first-person sleeve. The Army's uniform survey spans multiple periods: later M1943 clothing and M1944/M1945 equipment do not establish a universal August 1944 outfit. Officer and enlisted rank insignia must remain separate from divisional identity. The purchased paratrooper's exact unit and issued loadout remain unverified.

美军野战夹克、M1钢盔、携行具和有日期的军衔图用于外观比较。制服调查跨多个年代，不能把后期装备整套套用为1944年8月标准装束；军衔与师级徽记须分别核对。购买的伞兵模型所属单位与具体配发装备仍待证据确认。

The 1945 Allied handbook distinguishes German Heer uniforms, rank and branch markings. It is later than the Paris battle and is not an inventory of a particular garrison. Monochrome plates do not calibrate fabric or piping colors. British/Canadian sheets remain separate comparisons; they do not identify an American model.

1945年盟军手册可用于辨别德军陆军制服、军衔和兵种，但不能证明巴黎某守备单位的实际配装。黑白图不能作为布料或滚边颜色标定。英军、加拿大资料仅作独立比较，不代表美军角色。

Sources: U.S. Army uniform survey, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Survey_of_U.S._Army_Uniforms,_Weapons_and_Accoutrements_%282007%29,_by_David_Cole.pdf ; German handbook

note.zh: 复用制服与军衔辨别文字；原诺曼底单位和制作建议不作为巴黎角色的采用依据。
note.en: Reuse uniform and rank distinctions only; original Normandy unit assignments and production recommendations do not authorize Paris character adoption.

historical_references.title: Weapon appearance and game presentation / 枪械外观与游戏表现
historical_references.limitation: 原文研究记录；不等于资产采用或运行验收。 / Research notes; not asset adoption or runtime acceptance.
historical_references.excerpt:
# Weapon appearance and game presentation / 枪械外观与游戏表现

Distinguish M1 Garand, M1 Carbine and M1903-family forms and feeding arrangements. A clip-fed rifle must not be depicted with an unrelated detachable box magazine. German Kar98k-family silhouette and bolt-action presentation differ from submachine guns. Individual variant, sling, markings and unit issue require separate evidence; an equipment plate does not prove use on a specific Paris street.

区分M1加兰德、M1卡宾枪和M1903枪族的外形及供弹形式；弹夹供弹步枪不应显示无关的可拆弹匣。德军Kar98k枪族的轮廓与动作不能混同冲锋枪。具体子型、枪带、标记和配发单位仍需单独证据，装备图不能证明某条巴黎街道上的实际使用。

The weapon mesh, hands, visible feed component and ammunition counter should describe the same weapon. These are consistency checks for the existing rifle-resource design, not authorization to change accepted weapon/resource rules or a claim of new reload accuracy. Modern animation packs remain adaptation inputs; they are not historical evidence by themselves.

枪械网格、手部、可见供弹部件与弹药计数应相互一致。本条用于现有射击/装弹设计的表现核对，不授权修改已认可的资源规则，也不新增装弹准确性验收。现代动作包属于适配输入，本身不是历史证据。

Sources: U.S. Army uniform/equipment survey https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Survey_of_U.S._Army_Uniforms,_Weapons_and_Accoutrements_%282007%29,_by_David_Co

note.zh: 记录枪型、弹药与画面动作的一致性检查。旧诺曼底候选武器与制作规格不作为当前玩法要求。
note.en: Checks consistency among weapon family, ammunition and animation. Legacy Normandy weapon candidates and production specifications are not current gameplay requirements.

historical_references.excerpt:
# Weapon appearance and game presentation / 枪械外观与游戏表现

Distinguish M1 Garand, M1 Carbine and M1903-family forms and feeding arrangements. A clip-fed rifle must not be depicted with an unrelated detachable box magazine. German Kar98k-family silhouette and bolt-action presentation differ from submachine guns. Individual variant, sling, markings and unit issue require separate evidence; an equipment plate does not prove use on a specific Paris street.

区分M1加兰德、M1卡宾枪和M1903枪族的外形及供弹形式；弹夹供弹步枪不应显示无关的可拆弹匣。德军Kar98k枪族的轮廓与动作不能混同冲锋枪。具体子型、枪带、标记和配发单位仍需单独证据，装备图不能证明某条巴黎街道上的实际使用。

The weapon mesh, hands, visible feed component and ammunition counter should describe the same weapon. These are consistency checks for the existing rifle-resource design, not authorization to change accepted weapon/resource rules or a claim of new reload accuracy. Modern animation packs remain adaptation inputs; they are not historical evidence by themselves.

枪械网格、手部、可见供弹部件与弹药计数应相互一致。本条用于现有射击/装弹设计的表现核对，不授权修改已认可的资源规则，也不新增装弹准确性验收。现代动作包属于适配输入，本身不是历史证据。

Sources: U.S. Army uniform/equipment survey https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Survey_of_U.S._Army_Uniforms,_Weapons_and_Accoutrements_%282007%29,_by_David_Co

historical_references.excerpt:
# Paris, August 1944 - historical production context

## Narrative baseline

The playable encounter is fictionalized within the liberation period in August 1944. Normandy on 6 June supplies campaign background only. Avoid suggesting the player steps off a Normandy beach directly into Paris on the same day.

The Musee de la Liberation describes the uprising, resistance organization and barricades from 19 August through the 26 August parade; it records nearly 600 barricades in Paris and its nearby urban area on 24 August. These civic and resistance elements matter to the historical setting even when complex civilian simulation is out of production scope. [P01](https://www.museeliberation-leclerc-moulin.paris.fr/en/museum/la-liberation-de-paris)

The American 4th Infantry Division participated in the liberation of Paris and had landed at Utah Beach on D-Day. Selecting that formation would require correcting any inherited Omaha unit identity. The French 2nd Armored Division and FFI are separate identity/reference tracks; similar American-looking equipment does not establish unit affiliation. historical_references.excerpt:
# Mk II fragmentation grenade / Mk II破片手雷

The current game prop is the Mk II extracted from the licensed Allied equipment mesh, not a newly identified museum object. The 3 July 1942 War Department TM 9-1900, printed page 37, Figure 12 A, depicts the recognizable segmented exterior, top assembly and lever. The registered crop isolates that exterior view; no internal drawing or operating procedure is reproduced.

当前模型来自购买的盟军装备网格。1942年7月3日美军《TM 9-1900》印刷页37、图12 A可对照分块外壳、顶部轮廓和压柄。配图为原页外观图的局部裁切，不含内部结构或操作步骤。

The 1942 plate labels the Mk II body yellow. It is an earlier dated comparison, not evidence that every grenade in August 1944 Paris had that finish. The current game's paint, exact lot and unit issue have not been certified by this reference. Fragmentation damage, fuse timing, inventory and checkpoint rules remain game design decisions; this reference does not change them.

1942年图版标注黄色弹体；不能据此断定1944年8月巴黎所有手雷的涂装。当前模型涂装、批号与具体单位配发未由该资料确认。伤害、延时、库存和存档仍按现有游戏设计，不从外观图推导。

historical_references.title: AN-M8-inspired smoke grenade / AN-M8风格烟雾弹
historical_references.limitation: 原文研究记录；不等于资产采用或运行验收。 / Research notes; not asset adoption or runtime acceptance.
historical_references.excerpt:
# AN-M8-inspired smoke grenade / AN-M8风格烟雾弹

The current team-authored model is an AN-M8-inspired exterior. War Department TM 9-1981 dated 8 December 1943 identifies the white-smoke item in paragraph 36 (printed p48), and Figure 15 on printed p49 shows its exterior beside its fiber container. The visible reference supports a cylindrical body, top lever, gray finish, yellow band and HC/SMOKE identification. The local figure is the original exterior illustration, not a modern reenactment or M18 colored-smoke substitution.

当前模型为团队制作的AN-M8风格外观。1943年12月8日《TM 9-1981》第36节（印刷页48）及图15（印刷页49）提供圆柱罐体、顶部压柄、灰色涂装、黄色识别带及HC/SMOKE标记的依据。配图为原始外观图；右侧物体是纤维包装筒，不能当作第二枚烟雾弹。

The source establishes period appearance, not the exact issue to a Paris squad or the current art dimensions. Smoke concealment, world-space effects, duration and saved-resource behavior are game adaptations requiring their own validation. The manual's old health/safety statements are not current guidance and are not adopted in the app's summary. No mixture, internal construction or operating steps are reproduced.

资料支持当时外观，不证明巴黎某小队的具体配发，也不认证当前美术尺寸。烟幕遮蔽、世界空间效果、持续时间和存档资源属于游戏改编，须分别验证；不采用旧手册的健康与安全表述。

Primary source scan: https://www.bul

historical_references.title: Ammunition packing box / 弹药包装箱
historical_references.limitation: 原文研究记录；不等于资产采用或运行验收。 / Research notes; not asset adoption or runtime acceptance.
historical_references.excerpt:
# Ammunition packing box / 弹药包装箱

The game currently uses the Paris city pack's SM_AmmoBox_01a as the finite ammunition supply prop. Its exact historical box pattern, nation, contents and markings have not been identified. War Department TM 9-1900 dated 3 July 1942, printed p34 Figure 11 (PDF p35), provides a period comparison for small-arms ammunition packing boxes: wooden rectangular cases, carrying arrangements and stencilled caliber/content labels. The crop shows these exterior examples only.

当前补给道具采用巴黎城市包的SM_AmmoBox_01a；尚未确认它对应的具体历史箱型、国家、内容物与标记。1942年7月3日《TM 9-1900》印刷页34、图11（PDF页35）可对照轻武器弹药木箱的矩形箱体、提携结构及口径/内容物模板字。配图仅展示箱体外观。

The .30/.50 labels in the illustration identify those illustrated containers, not the contents of the game prop or a match to the player's rifle. Do not label a generic vendor mesh as a verified M1917/M1 box without a matching object record. The game supply remains a finite interaction with existing inventory conservation; it does not automatically contain medicine, refill on saving or establish historical resupply rates.

图中.30/.50字样只说明图示包装，不能当作游戏箱内实际弹药或玩家步枪适配证明。没有匹配证据，不把通用供应商网格标为已核实的M1917/M1箱。游戏仍采用有限库存与原弹药守恒规则；不自动提供药品，不因存档补满。

Primary source scan: https:/

historical_references.excerpt:
# Paris, August 1944 - historical production context

## Narrative baseline

The playable encounter is fictionalized within the liberation period in August 1944. Normandy on 6 June supplies campaign background only. Avoid suggesting the player steps off a Normandy beach directly into Paris on the same day.

The Musee de la Liberation describes the uprising, resistance organization and barricades from 19 August through the 26 August parade; it records nearly 600 barricades in Paris and its nearby urban area on 24 August. These civic and resistance elements matter to the historical setting even when complex civilian simulation is out of production scope. [P01](https://www.museeliberation-leclerc-moulin.paris.fr/en/museum/la-liberation-de-paris)

The American 4th Infantry Division participated in the liberation of Paris and had landed at Utah Beach on D-Day. Selecting that formation would require correcting any inherited Omaha unit identity. The French 2nd Armored Division and FFI are separate identity/reference tracks; similar American-looking equipment does not establish unit affiliation. historical_references.excerpt:
# V10 references and decisions

2026-10-04. Reopened all four museum_001–004 images under the original private pilot references. Source Paris Musées collection 2019.1.1 / record860143 (URL recorded in ../GermanRiflePilot/reference_notes.md), same1943 specimen, CC0 per preserved caption. Whole opposing sides show butt–curved wrist–long continuous lower fore-end, upper wood stopping near forward band, slender exposed muzzle, round open guard, downturned right bolt. historical_references.excerpt:
# Ammunition packing box / 弹药包装箱

The game currently uses the Paris city pack's SM_AmmoBox_01a as the finite ammunition supply prop. Its exact historical box pattern, nation, contents and markings have not been identified. War Department TM 9-1900 dated 3 July 1942, printed p34 Figure 11 (PDF p35), provides a period comparison for small-arms ammunition packing boxes: wooden rectangular cases, carrying arrangements and stencilled caliber/content labels. The crop shows these exterior examples only.

当前补给道具采用巴黎城市包的SM_AmmoBox_01a；尚未确认它对应的具体历史箱型、国家、内容物与标记。1942年7月3日《TM 9-1900》印刷页34、图11（PDF页35）可对照轻武器弹药木箱的矩形箱体、提携结构及口径/内容物模板字。配图仅展示箱体外观。

The .30/.50 labels in the illustration identify those illustrated containers, not the contents of the game prop or a match to the player's rifle. Do not label a generic vendor mesh as a verified M1917/M1 box without a matching object record. The game supply remains a finite interaction with existing inventory conservation; it does not automatically contain medicine, refill on saving or establish historical resupply rates.

图中.30/.50字样只说明图示包装，不能当作游戏箱内实际弹药或玩家步枪适配证明。没有匹配证据，不把通用供应商网格标为已核实的M1917/M1箱。游戏仍采用有限库存与原弹药守恒规则；不自动提供药品，不因存档补满。

Primary source scan: https:/

historical_references.excerpt:
# Paris, August 1944 - historical production context

## Narrative baseline

The playable encounter is fictionalized within the liberation period in August 1944. Normandy on 6 June supplies campaign background only. Avoid suggesting the player steps off a Normandy beach directly into Paris on the same day.

The Musee de la Liberation describes the uprising, resistance organization and barricades from 19 August through the 26 August parade; it records nearly 600 barricades in Paris and its nearby urban area on 24 August. These civic and resistance elements matter to the historical setting even when complex civilian simulation is out of production scope. [P01](https://www.museeliberation-leclerc-moulin.paris.fr/en/museum/la-liberation-de-paris)

The American 4th Infantry Division participated in the liberation of Paris and had landed at Utah Beach on D-Day. Selecting that formation would require correcting any inherited Omaha unit identity. The French 2nd Armored Division and FFI are separate identity/reference tracks; similar American-looking equipment does not establish unit affiliation. [P03](https://achh.army.mil/history/book-wwii-huertgenforest-4thidsurgannual1944/) and [P04](ht

## Narrative baseline

The playable encounter is fictionalized within the liberation period in August 1944. Normandy on 6 June supplies campaign background only. Avoid suggesting the player steps off a Normandy beach directly into Paris on the same day.

The Musee de la Liberation describes the uprising, resistance organization and barricades from 19 August through the 26 August parade; it records nearly 600 barricades in Paris and its nearby urban area on 24 August. The American 4th Infantry Division participated in the liberation of Paris and had landed at Utah Beach on D-Day. Selecting that formation would require correcting any inherited Omaha unit identity. The French 2nd Armored Division and FFI are separate identity/reference tracks; similar American-looking equipment does not establish unit affiliation. historical_references.excerpt:
# Paris, August 1944 - historical production context

## Narrative baseline

The playable encounter is fictionalized within the liberation period in August 1944. Normandy on 6 June supplies campaign background only. Avoid suggesting the player steps off a Normandy beach directly into Paris on the same day.

The Musee de la Liberation describes the uprising, resistance organization and barricades from 19 August through the 26 August parade; it records nearly 600 barricades in Paris and its nearby urban area on 24 August. These civic and resistance elements matter to the historical setting even when complex civilian simulation is out of production scope. [P01](https://www.museeliberation-leclerc-moulin.paris.fr/en/museum/la-liberation-de-paris)

The American 4th Infantry Division participated in the liberation of Paris and had landed at Utah Beach on D-Day. Selecting that formation would require correcting any inherited Omaha unit identity. The French 2nd Armored Division and FFI are separate identity/reference tracks; similar American-looking equipment does not establish unit affiliation. historical_references.excerpt:
# WWII medical bag — real-photo material audit

17 October 2026. Human asks for a real WWII medical bag after finding the current candidate texture unconvincing. Reference research/source diagnosis only; no model, texture, game or save writes. The accepted shape remains intact; v2 material needs revision and has no human acceptance.

## Sources actually examined

1. 1944 Militaria, “Original US WWII Medic's Bag Dated 1941 With Contents”: https://www.1944militaria.com/Original_US_WWII_Medics_Bag_With_Contents_p/orusmedbg1.htm . This is the dealer's identification/date, not independent authentication. Description records staining/soiling, hardware corrosion and intact cloth. Inspected its actual 1000×666 photograph in the browser: https://www.1944militaria.com/v/vspfiles/photos/ORUSMEDBG1-2.jpg . Visible front, top rim, closure webbing, shoulder strap, hardware and lower lacing. Use as close material/reference photography, not a photo texture source or provenance proof for the game.
2. Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, collection record nasm_A19720895000, “Kit, First Aid, United States Army Air Forces”: https://www.si.edu/object/nasm_A19720895000 . Record describes green cot

note.en: Appearance selection and provenance review for finite medical kits. Museum-label attribution and dealer dating remain qualified; the candidate model is not adopted and gameplay is unimplemented.

historical_references.excerpt:
Actual images opened in the browser, not merely search snippets:

- Paris Musées, Musée Jean Moulin: [M-1942 first aid packet pouch](https://www.parismuseescollections.paris.fr/fr/musee-jean-moulin/oeuvres/us-pouch-first-aid-packet-m-1942-british-made), image lpdp_203720-16.jpg. Compact single-snap envelope with diagonal flap edges, gathered cloth at corners, belt fittings. Museum image is front-facing and does not determine our depth or rear construction. Primary page fetch timed out; image opened. Do not claim unverified catalogue details.
- [IMCS shell dressing bag](https://www.imcsmilitaria.com/shop.php?code=69788), image69788b.jpg. Visually reviewed oblique image: broad soft rectangular filled bag, rounded top fold, wrapping flap, two spaced narrow webbing closures/buckles, circular faded medical mark. Main construction analogue; dealer dating is not direct historical evidence. Our compact proportions/back loops are adaptations, not inferred hidden geometry.
- [Foxhole M1942 pouch](https://www.foxholemilitaria.com/product-page/u-s-m-1942-first-aid-pouch-wwii), image7722e6_c9bc8b44838645c48802f77170d63511. Close front shows woven cloth, folded top, sagged flap point, thick stit

research.title: Paris, August 1944 - historical production context
research.body:
# Paris, August 1944 - historical production context

## Narrative baseline

The playable encounter is fictionalized within the liberation period in August 1944. Normandy on 6 June supplies campaign background only. Avoid suggesting the player steps off a Normandy beach directly into Paris on the same day.

The Musee de la Liberation describes the uprising, resistance organization and barricades from 19 August through the 26 August parade; it records nearly 600 barricades in Paris and its nearby urban area on 24 August. These civic and resistance elements matter to the historical setting even when complex civilian simulation is out of production scope. [P01](https://www.museeliberation-leclerc-moulin.paris.fr/en/museum/la-liberation-de-paris)

The American 4th Infantry Division participated in the liberation of Paris and had landed at Utah Beach on D-Day. Selecting that formation would require correcting any inherited Omaha unit identity. The French 2nd Armored Division and FFI are separate identity/reference tracks; similar American-looking equipment does not establish unit affiliation. [P03](https://achh.army.mil/history/book-wwii-huertgenforest-4thidsurgannual1944/) and [P04](https://www.army.mil/article/165476/1st_sbct_honors_crossing_of_the_rhine_river)

No player unit or enemy formation is selected by this document. Choose identities alongside compatible licensed assets, then verify uniforms, insignia and weapons. Do not invent a documented combat event for a fictionalized asset-pack street.

## Street and environment use

The Paris municipal event map provides locations and episodes for reference, including command posts, barricades and the Grand Palais. Use it to distinguish actual sites from the asset pack's generic city composition. [P02](https://www.paris.fr/en/pages/relive-the-liberation-of-paris-through-an-interactive-map-36122)

The Paris Musees collection entry for a barricade at rue de la Huchette / place du Petit-Pont is dated 23 August 1944. It is a useful date-and-place-specific visual reference, not evidence for the layout of every Paris street. [P05](https://parismuseescollections.paris.fr/en/node/132774)

Buildings, posters, street signs, civilian vehicles, tank variants, rubble density, flags and military insignia need a selected-scene review. Do not use aircraft/paratrooper VFX from the environment package simply because it contains them. Limit alterations to historical mismatches visible in the bounded encounter rather than reconstructing Paris.

## Weather and time

Use fixed lighting. No precise date-specific temperature, humidity, wind or rain values have been established in this source set. Keep them unknown. Normandy D-Day weather and the film Pressure are not evidence for August Paris conditions.

## Evidence standard

Record title, institution, event date/location, URL, image rights and limitations. Distinguish fighting photographs from celebrations, later photographs, reenactments and asset marketing. Do not infer a unit, weapon variant, exact street geometry or meteorological reading from an ambiguous image. Preserve the distinction between historical inspiration and verified reconstruction in the final presentation.

research.title: V15 references and diagnosis — 2026-10-04
research.body:
# V15 references and diagnosis — 2026-10-04

Actually inspected original M1 wood patch (723×434 at569,76–1292,510), V14 stock,
four V15 preview views and two independently reviewed stock/handguard/unlit sets.
Existing licensed/private M1 atlas and scene read-only; no download/new imagery.

Source main.py V12 and V10 loft verify mapping: UV U=(designX+.379)/1.105. One
723-pixel crop therefore spans1.105m; old1K→2K resampling supplies no new native
grain. Read-only GLB diagnosis measures stock U0–.873303 / .965m (~631source
columns), handguard U.574661–.866063/.322m (~210sourcecolumns). Existing standard
linear sampling isn't the primary cause; it is density plus chained sampling.

Fixed4×longitudinal native high-frequency sampling gives~2614sourcepx/m, rather
than simply sharpening old blurred data. Keep approved V14 macro appearance,
same source registration for colour/normal/roughness, correct mirrored normal
directions. Dark mean colour after PNG drifts at most.016% in preview; not a
visual acceptance metric. No source positional AO/large curvature transfer.

Preview visual review: finer stock grain is genuinely readable, also unlit.
Handguard gains detail mainly on its brown strip; pale grazing highlights still
wash out other faces. Old broad stretched/mirrored motifs remain, source grain
detail can read dense/broken, not a full bespoke M1 scratch/edge artwork. No
obvious hard new seam in inspected views. Final11source/8fresh and fixed matched
sheet/native crop corroborate; independent eight-image review agrees. All
parameters unchanged from early proof; no corrective appearance round. Stock
benefit is visible but M1 remains richer/sharper. No claim of M1 equivalence,
historical certification, rights/release, UE mip/shimmer/FPS. Last pass stopped.

# V7 reference / review observations

Read main Blender modeling skill and all four references; project HANDOFF, Failures index, GP001–005, V5/V6 results. Existing CC0 Paris museum Kar98k2019.1.1 top/underside photographs reviewed again. Existing reference page/photo provenance lives in the pilot; no new web/cloud transaction.

Reference mechanical relationships: steel receiver lies narrowly inside the wood shoulders, cylindrical receiver rings have coherent transitions; rear sight leaf/slider are flat manufactured surfaces rather than amorphous lumps; trigger guard/underside plate are steel, but a sling can obscure them. Museum replacement sling is not an accepted issued1944 sling.

Named fixed orthographic cameras in common.py reuse the source pose and remain fixed through before/after/fresh comparison. Compare the same whole side, receiver quarter and top. No overlay/IoU/landmark metric claimed; referenced comparison tools are not exposed in this session. Complementary sides/top/bottom/reverse/muzzle inspected. Gray normals repair visibly improves wood and receiver highlights without moving vertices. PBR own-atlas still looks soft/melted in close views. Surface_v1/v2 cyan proves missed hardware and false assignments; it is not a final material.

research.title: Reference and finish observations
research.body:
# Reference and finish observations

User explicitly lowers finish to ordinary Allied M1 world-prop level: coherent silhouette, readable metal/wood, round barrel and supported sight; not engraving, manufacture accuracy or complete operating internals. M1 reference has3,923triangles and D/N/ORM2048²; its proportions, commercial atlas and grip/rig remain protected, not copied. Current Kar inherits296,719triangles from the dense original: **not similarly optimized/game-ready**.

Existing museum top/right/left/bottom photographs and V7 matched evidence, as recorded in earlier reference study, remain the comparison set; no new external image/cloud call. The V7 muzzle has multiple soft upright protrusions, broad lumpy crown and indistinct opening. V9 explicitly authored paired-root barrel, annular crown and one supported tapered blade remove these conspicuous front defects. Actual gray whole-right/left/top/bottom, muzzle side/top/forward/reverse inspected; original stock/sling and repaired ball remain. At game-prop distance the new front is regular; reverse view resolves a genuine bore, not a painted dark disc.

PBR shows an obvious boundary between new blued steel and the source's beige/soft material response. Original fore-end hardware, receiver/sight/safety remain lumpy. Do not call the whole rifle M1-equivalent finish or hide this contrast with another unproved semantic paint pass. Blade/base are static and simplified; no matching front/rear sight line, rig, bolt/reload animation or historical variant certification. Minor engravings intentionally excluded; large material/shape integration is not an excluded micro detail.

GP008 stops receiver skin after post-subdivision edge-incidence failure despite successful manual boundary unfolding. Next receiver method requires explicit conforming topology without that failed edge subdivider, or finished compatible content. No second correction/contour sweep within this package. Deliver only the independently verified joined-front candidate and accurate remaining gaps.

research.title: Kar98k reference and modeling contract
research.body:
# Kar98k reference and modeling contract

2026-10-03. Stage 1 reviewed; isolated world-prop pilot, not a historical loadout or UE selection.

## Source and observed form

[Paris Musées record 860143](https://parismuseescollections.paris.fr/en/node/860143): 1943 Mauser Kar98k, collection 2019.1.1, associated with the Senate / Luxembourg Garden liberation. Four original photographs and the downloaded caption explicitly identify the photographs as CC0. Credit Paris Musées / Musée de la Libération de Paris – musée du général Leclerc – musée Jean Moulin. No purchased commercial files or private material will be sent to Aholo.

Originals under the pilot `references/originals/` were opened and inspected: 1736206 (left full side), 1736212 (right full side, bolt visible), 1736128 (receiver/bolt/sight top detail), 1736089 (underside plate/guard detail). Each is 8204×4965. The original ZIP and caption are preserved. Reference stage has opposing full side and close top/bottom coverage; there is no whole-rifle three-quarter photograph. Inspect generated depth from complementary rendered angles rather than inventing historical certainty.

The observed stock has a broad tapered butt, narrow curved wrist, continuous slender fore-end, reddish worn wood and distinct metal bands. The exposed front barrel is slender; receiver sits above the stock, with a visible downturned ball-ended handle on the right. The underside guard is open, not solid. The rear sight is a separate raised tangent form. Metal and wood boundaries must remain readable on both sides and top.

Record length 110.5 cm supplies an approximate full-body scale; recorded width/thickness include this specimen's accessories and are not bare-stock engineering dimensions. The museum notes missing cleaning rod and sight hood and a replaced British Sten canvas sling. This trial may reflect missing hood/rod; its sling is a museum-condition feature, not approved German-issued equipment. Omit the sling only if separable without destructive core loss. Do not invent precision or real internal mechanisms.

## Contract / gates

- Target: smooth textured Kar98k appearance for German NPC world use; provisional scale 1.105 m, evaluated triangle ceiling 30k only after silhouette approval.
- Parts: continuous wood stock/handguard; recognizable receiver and front barrel; front/rear sight; open trigger guard; identifiable separate visual bolt/handle. Neither matched hand animation nor internal operating accuracy is required.
- Preserve downloaded base and existing game/character/gun bytes. Work only in `Assets/LocalWorking/Experiments/GermanRiflePilot/20261003-v1/`.
- One G1 image-to-3D base request using right-side then opposite-side original photos, faceCount300000, outputFormat GLB, aiPredictSize=false. G1 PBR is intrinsic; enablePbr is forbidden by its current official contract. No additional segmentation/articulation calls.
- Live API balance260 reconciles prior 300 gift minus two20 jobs. Gift expiry is not exposed by the balance contract; usable balance is live, no paid credits/top-ups known. Quote must be ≤20 and account unchanged before submission. Preserve attempted submission before calling; never blindly retry.
- Stage 2/3 early gate: inspect both sides/top/three-quarter, shape and negative spaces with neutral geometry views separately from PBR. A failed core form stops after the one job. At most two bounded Blender repairs if the primary form passes. No offset/parameter search campaign.
- Final local delivery only if shape, parts, UV/material/texture, scale, normals, export, clean re-import and visible digital pivot checks pass. Required matching evidence views and durable deterministic adaptation script; no UE/game acceptance from import alone.

## Failure handling

Read FP001 analysis and stopped character pilot records: neither successful numerical checks nor expensive repeated changes establish visual quality. Reserve cloud state before mutation, retain source/output hashes and failed evidence. Unknown billing/submission stops dispatch. Failed forms stop this candidate; do not replace it with a disguised blockout. No SFTP publication, Catalog change, purchase, M1 reload repair or Git push.

research.title: V10 references and decisions
research.body:
# V10 references and decisions

2026-10-04. Reopened all four museum_001–004 images under the original private pilot references. Source Paris Musées collection 2019.1.1 / record860143 (URL recorded in ../GermanRiflePilot/reference_notes.md), same1943 specimen, CC0 per preserved caption. Whole opposing sides show butt–curved wrist–long continuous lower fore-end, upper wood stopping near forward band, slender exposed muzzle, round open guard, downturned right bolt. Top/bottom detail distinguishes the supported tangent sight and steel floorplate. Museum sling is replacement, omitted in this new separable model; no hood/cleaning rod invented as required details. No calibrated full three-quarter reference. Length110.5cm is approximate, not manufacturing specification.

Source donor is modern SP-R208, not historical proof. Source diagnosis inspected eight individual mesh views and all component bounds/weights. Mesh_0.070 is synthetic stock and is excluded entirely. Mesh_1.034 has2070-face lower receiver component and1586-face distinct top rail; retain component0 only after actually seeing both. Mesh_2.025 is forward synthetic shroud, excluded. Mesh_3.020 is bolt tube/safety; Mesh_0.073 is bolt handle/cap/pin; Mesh_4.017 component1 is trigger, component0 is detachable-mag release and excluded. Mesh_5.011 modern fasteners/sight bits excluded. Barrel Mesh_0.074 and muzzle insert Mesh_1.035 retained. No semantic coordinate classifier, cut or hull is used. Diagnosis groups exactly coincident vertices only for component graph, never welds source geometry.

Normalize world coordinates around receiver rearX=-240.204742cm, barrel axisY≈-.2615cm/Z≈18.30cm; +X muzzle. New wood buttX≈-.379m, tip≈.726m. Stock groove follows separately measured receiver/barrel radius; two lower/upper wood halves are clamped by bands. New stock station positions are author-selected from the observed silhouette, not photo-calibrated ground truth. Ordinary Allied prop is finish reference, not copied model/atlas. Retain donor UV and authored normals for extracted metal, use new baked wood atlases; modern receiver/extractor/safety differences remain historical limitations until separate review.

research.title: V8 references / assumptions
research.body:
# V8 references / assumptions

Existing same1943 museum Kar98k2019.1.1 CC0 series from https://parismuseescollections.paris.fr/en/node/860143. Original locally stored full sides1736212/1736206 and top1736128/underside1736089 under20261003-v1/references/originals. No new proprietary image upload or material reuse. Photos are perspective, not calibrated drawings; provisional source dimensions stay unchanged.

Receiver follows the barrel axis inside retained wood shoulders. Cylindrical rings/bolt cap need clean curves and deliberate transitions, not white soft blobs. Rear sight has an inclined leaf with supported base and rectangular sliding hardware; it is not a long modern accessory rail. Front sight/muzzle should have proper barrel bore and slim supported blade; this museum example lacks a hood/cleaning rod, not general variant approval. Museum replacement sling remains an open historical limitation.

Primary gate is actual original-mesh interface, not decorative detail. Hand-picked surface landmarks must lead to a simple continuous original-edge loop before topology replacement. V7 fixed cameras retained for genuine before/after comparisons. Compare both steel interiors and wood shoulders, not only top silhouette. No unavailable overlay/IoU tool or manufactured dimensional accuracy claim.

Actual outcome: original-edge156 proof alone insufficient: top projection crosses and region has an exactly coincident four-face edge. V8/V8B stopped without source replacement (GP007). V8C outputs **standalone** analytical receiver/sight/muzzle objects in a provisional sloped frame. Its own cameras review only those parts; they are NOT same-whole-rifle before/after evidence. Safety flag is static neutral approximation, notch simplified two-shoulder gap, sight scale rails have no engraved numbers. No handle/stock/sling integration or dimensional certification. Source preservation does not establish interface acceptance.

research.title: Pressure mine exterior references, 11 October 2026
research.body:
# Pressure mine exterior references, 11 October 2026

Use is private visual observation only. None of the reference pixels are a game texture or public document illustration.

- [Smithsonian object record](https://americanhistory.si.edu/collections/object/nmah_407167): search-index record describes a flattened circular metal case and side carry handle. Direct page fetch was blocked (403); no Smithsonian image inspection claimed.
- [IMA inert T.Mi.35 training prop](https://www.ima-usa.com/products/original-u-s-wwii-german-anti-tank-tellermine-t-mi-35-training-mine?variant=14045816062021), observed `ON7001__07_1024x1024.jpg`: oblique low side, broad circular body, rounded rolled edges and gently convex top. Surface has mottled paint/rust/chips; no sharp faceted primitive silhouette.
- [IMA inert T.Mi.42 training prop](https://www.ima-usa.com/products/original-u-s-wwii-german-anti-tank-tellermine-t-mi-42-training-mine?variant=31166743642181), observed `ONSV3266__04.jpg`: lower side, raised stepped pressure plate, supported side loop and continuous thin seam. Hierarchy is low body plus narrower upper plate, rather than three tall square posts.
- [Australian War Memorial S Mi 35](https://www.awm.gov.au/collection/C326811), observed `3831511.JPG`: tall cylinder, dark worn green metal and actual rounded hardware. This cylinder is an analogue for finish only; its taller silhouette is deliberately not used for the requested readable disc.

Model is a fictional exterior-only WWII-style game prop with a personnel-contact trigger. It does not reproduce internal construction or certify a particular historic weapon; anti-tank exterior references do not establish the game's foot-trigger rule. No executable mechanisms are modeled.

Geometry v1 inspection: low disc, stepped plate, continuous seam and supported loop are visible in matching side/oblique/top views; silhouette no longer resembles the rejected upright gray cylinder. Studio exposure was too bright and the initial stencil intersected the sloped shoulder. Preserve v1. V2 changes only studio exposure and places the stencil on the flat upper plate; surface finish gets restrained curvature wear. Inspect the new images before texture/export/runtime integration.

research.title: WWII medical bag — real-photo material audit
research.body:
# WWII medical bag — real-photo material audit

17 October 2026. Human asks for a real WWII medical bag after finding the current candidate texture unconvincing. Reference research/source diagnosis only; no model, texture, game or save writes. The accepted shape remains intact; v2 material needs revision and has no human acceptance.

## Sources actually examined

1. 1944 Militaria, “Original US WWII Medic's Bag Dated 1941 With Contents”: https://www.1944militaria.com/Original_US_WWII_Medics_Bag_With_Contents_p/orusmedbg1.htm . This is the dealer's identification/date, not independent authentication. Description records staining/soiling, hardware corrosion and intact cloth. Inspected its actual 1000×666 photograph in the browser: https://www.1944militaria.com/v/vspfiles/photos/ORUSMEDBG1-2.jpg . Visible front, top rim, closure webbing, shoulder strap, hardware and lower lacing. Use as close material/reference photography, not a photo texture source or provenance proof for the game.
2. Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, collection record nasm_A19720895000, “Kit, First Aid, United States Army Air Forces”: https://www.si.edu/object/nasm_A19720895000 . Record describes green cotton canvas, two brown cloth straps and a hand-painted red cross, and associates the object with WWII B-24 gunner Walter Kramer. Visited the actual live record and enlarged its image in the browser. Caution: the visible image includes a display label with a different inventory/donor than the record; do not assert that the pictured specimen is the same individual object or copy its attribution. Use the collection record to corroborate material vocabulary and the image only for visible cloth/strap/paint appearance. Image usage restrictions apply; no source media downloaded, adopted or uploaded.
3. Reading Museum, “Second World War medical kit”, H97F: https://collections.readingmuseum.org.uk/pdfs/H97F.pdf . Read the museum's record: dated 1939 inside, used during WWII by Mr Treacher and donated in 1984. Confirms durable canvas with straps and metal buckles. PDF screenshot was attempted through web, but no visible image was delivered in that tool response; do not claim a visual fabric inspection from that attempt. British example is corroboration, not the current US design authority.

Web image searches also surfaced modern reproductions and M1945 cargo bags; neither was selected as the Paris1944 material/design baseline. No full-resolution original media was saved locally in this audit; sources above remain remote, and the existing local model evidence is unchanged.

## Comparison and source causes

Actually inspected current v2 DETAIL.jpg and the real-photo views above. Visual observations/inferences, not lab textile measurements:

- Real body cloth reads as dense interlaced canvas, with small irregular fibers/threads. Current body has conspicuous soft square repetition and reads as a smooth surface with a coarse grid. Avoid simply increasing normal strength: the interlacing/profile itself needs repair.
- Real closure/shoulder webbing has a visibly different, coarser and more directional structure from the pouch body. Source create_medkit.py textured_cloth uses the same 64-cycle cosine height function for both materials; original canvas/webbing normal PNG bytes are identical (confirmed by hash). Different colours alone do not establish different textiles.
- Current weather_medkit.py v2 retains those normals and largely adds broad spatial noise plus a lower-height dirt mask and short AO. It therefore changes colour/weathering without fixing the shared weave. Current v2 dirt is too broadly cloudy and generic. Real photo shows seam/rim/strap wear and discrete handling spots; weathering should depend more on construction/contact regions, with less face-wide gray clouding.
- Real fabric looks warm khaki/olive under its photograph, while v2 appears somewhat gray and chalky in the studio. This is a visual direction only: differing lighting/white balance cannot establish exact historical colour values. Preserve a coherent cloth dye base while varying worn fiber and local dirt, instead of globally desaturating the whole bag.
- Current red marking loses colour through isotropic fine-noise speckles. The museum photo shows irregular hand-applied paint interacting with woven cloth. A later marking pass should retain the accepted patch design but derive loss/penetration from fibers and local abrasion, with fewer uniform dots. Do not infer every WWII marking was hand painted or identical to this example.

## Bounded next revision direction

Keep accepted geometry/UVs and all action/save/game authority. Make separate body-canvas and warp-dominant webbing normals/materials, with finer irregular body weave and directional strap ribs; avoid inventing an exact yarn density from unscaled images. Preserve mid-scale natural dye variation, reduce broad gray noise, localize soiling to seams/edge folds/strap contact and hardware, and add restrained fiber-based wear. Match the previous fixed lighting/camera for local before/after evidence. Replacing the old normal textures needs a new explicit material contract; the prior “normal pixels exact” check is not evidence of textile realism and should not constrain an authorized correction. No such material edit has yet been made in this audit.

Original v4 and weathering v1/v2 artifacts remain retained. Existing source/material manifests remain valid. No native import, Game compile/package/engine entry, asset-library/Catalog/index/SFTP adoption, action edits or save writes. The earlier smoke playtest request remains separately pending.

research.title: Medical kit — construction references
research.body:
Actual images opened in the browser, not merely search snippets:

- Paris Musées, Musée Jean Moulin: [M-1942 first aid packet pouch](https://www.parismuseescollections.paris.fr/fr/musee-jean-moulin/oeuvres/us-pouch-first-aid-packet-m-1942-british-made), image lpdp_203720-16.jpg. Compact single-snap envelope with diagonal flap edges, gathered cloth at corners, belt fittings. Museum image is front-facing and does not determine our depth or rear construction. Primary page fetch timed out; image opened. Do not claim unverified catalogue details.
- [IMCS shell dressing bag](https://www.imcsmilitaria.com/shop.php?code=69788), image69788b.jpg. Visually reviewed oblique image: broad soft rectangular filled bag, rounded top fold, wrapping flap, two spaced narrow webbing closures/buckles, circular faded medical mark. Main construction analogue; dealer dating is not direct historical evidence. Our compact proportions/back loops are adaptations, not inferred hidden geometry.
- [Foxhole M1942 pouch](https://www.foxholemilitaria.com/product-page/u-s-m-1942-first-aid-pouch-wwii), image7722e6_c9bc8b44838645c48802f77170d63511. Close front shows woven cloth, folded top, sagged flap point, thick stitched binding and aged metal snap. Construction/material reference only; not an additional view of the same object.

Reference images stay remote, with source links/observations recorded; no reference photography is redistributed or baked into the model. No purchase or external asset intake.

research.title: Uniforms, ranks and identity / 制服、军衔与身份
research.body:
# Uniforms, ranks and identity / 制服、军衔与身份

U.S. field jackets, M1 helmets, web equipment and dated rank plates provide appearance comparisons for the Allied soldier and first-person sleeve. The Army's uniform survey spans multiple periods: later M1943 clothing and M1944/M1945 equipment do not establish a universal August 1944 outfit. Officer and enlisted rank insignia must remain separate from divisional identity. The purchased paratrooper's exact unit and issued loadout remain unverified.

美军野战夹克、M1钢盔、携行具和有日期的军衔图用于外观比较。制服调查跨多个年代，不能把后期装备整套套用为1944年8月标准装束；军衔与师级徽记须分别核对。购买的伞兵模型所属单位与具体配发装备仍待证据确认。

The 1945 Allied handbook distinguishes German Heer uniforms, rank and branch markings. It is later than the Paris battle and is not an inventory of a particular garrison. Monochrome plates do not calibrate fabric or piping colors. British/Canadian sheets remain separate comparisons; they do not identify an American model.

1945年盟军手册可用于辨别德军陆军制服、军衔和兵种，但不能证明巴黎某守备单位的实际配装。黑白图不能作为布料或滚边颜色标定。英军、加拿大资料仅作独立比较，不代表美军角色。

Sources: U.S. Army uniform survey, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Survey_of_U.S._Army_Uniforms,_Weapons_and_Accoutrements_%282007%29,_by_David_Cole.pdf ; German handbook Chapter IX, https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USA/ref/TM/pdfs/TME30-451.PDF . Original source-register URLs, dates, archived scans and page locators remain in each linked source/image record. This cleaned equipment note replaces the inactive scenario-specific production sheet; it authorizes no character changes or adoption.

research.title: Weapon appearance and game presentation / 枪械外观与游戏表现
research.body:
# Weapon appearance and game presentation / 枪械外观与游戏表现

Distinguish M1 Garand, M1 Carbine and M1903-family forms and feeding arrangements. A clip-fed rifle must not be depicted with an unrelated detachable box magazine. German Kar98k-family silhouette and bolt-action presentation differ from submachine guns. Individual variant, sling, markings and unit issue require separate evidence; an equipment plate does not prove use on a specific Paris street.

区分M1加兰德、M1卡宾枪和M1903枪族的外形及供弹形式；弹夹供弹步枪不应显示无关的可拆弹匣。德军Kar98k枪族的轮廓与动作不能混同冲锋枪。具体子型、枪带、标记和配发单位仍需单独证据，装备图不能证明某条巴黎街道上的实际使用。

The weapon mesh, hands, visible feed component and ammunition counter should describe the same weapon. These are consistency checks for the existing rifle-resource design, not authorization to change accepted weapon/resource rules or a claim of new reload accuracy. Modern animation packs remain adaptation inputs; they are not historical evidence by themselves.

枪械网格、手部、可见供弹部件与弹药计数应相互一致。本条用于现有射击/装弹设计的表现核对，不授权修改已认可的资源规则，也不新增装弹准确性验收。现代动作包属于适配输入，本身不是历史证据。

Sources: U.S. Army uniform/equipment survey https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Survey_of_U.S._Army_Uniforms,_Weapons_and_Accoutrements_%282007%29,_by_David_Cole.pdf ; wartime equipment handbook https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USA/ref/TM/pdfs/TME30-451.PDF . Exact original plate locators and caveats remain in linked records. No internal construction or real-world operating procedure is reproduced here.

research.title: Mk II fragmentation grenade / Mk II破片手雷
research.body:
# Mk II fragmentation grenade / Mk II破片手雷

The current game prop is the Mk II extracted from the licensed Allied equipment mesh, not a newly identified museum object. The 3 July 1942 War Department TM 9-1900, printed page 37, Figure 12 A, depicts the recognizable segmented exterior, top assembly and lever. The registered crop isolates that exterior view; no internal drawing or operating procedure is reproduced.

当前模型来自购买的盟军装备网格。1942年7月3日美军《TM 9-1900》印刷页37、图12 A可对照分块外壳、顶部轮廓和压柄。配图为原页外观图的局部裁切，不含内部结构或操作步骤。

The 1942 plate labels the Mk II body yellow. It is an earlier dated comparison, not evidence that every grenade in August 1944 Paris had that finish. The current game's paint, exact lot and unit issue have not been certified by this reference. Fragmentation damage, fuse timing, inventory and checkpoint rules remain game design decisions; this reference does not change them.

1942年图版标注黄色弹体；不能据此断定1944年8月巴黎所有手雷的涂装。当前模型涂装、批号与具体单位配发未由该资料确认。伤害、延时、库存和存档仍按现有游戏设计，不从外观图推导。

Primary source scan: https://stephentaylorhistorian.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/tm-9-1900-ammunition-general-1942.pdf#page=38

research.title: AN-M8-inspired smoke grenade / AN-M8风格烟雾弹
research.body:
# AN-M8-inspired smoke grenade / AN-M8风格烟雾弹

The current team-authored model is an AN-M8-inspired exterior. War Department TM 9-1981 dated 8 December 1943 identifies the white-smoke item in paragraph 36 (printed p48), and Figure 15 on printed p49 shows its exterior beside its fiber container. The visible reference supports a cylindrical body, top lever, gray finish, yellow band and HC/SMOKE identification. The local figure is the original exterior illustration, not a modern reenactment or M18 colored-smoke substitution.

当前模型为团队制作的AN-M8风格外观。1943年12月8日《TM 9-1981》第36节（印刷页48）及图15（印刷页49）提供圆柱罐体、顶部压柄、灰色涂装、黄色识别带及HC/SMOKE标记的依据。配图为原始外观图；右侧物体是纤维包装筒，不能当作第二枚烟雾弹。

The source establishes period appearance, not the exact issue to a Paris squad or the current art dimensions. Smoke concealment, world-space effects, duration and saved-resource behavior are game adaptations requiring their own validation. The manual's old health/safety statements are not current guidance and are not adopted in the app's summary. No mixture, internal construction or operating steps are reproduced.

资料支持当时外观，不证明巴黎某小队的具体配发，也不认证当前美术尺寸。烟幕遮蔽、世界空间效果、持续时间和存档资源属于游戏改编，须分别验证；不采用旧手册的健康与安全表述。

Primary source scan: https://www.bulletpicker.com/pdf/TM-9-1981-1943.pdf#page=52

research.title: Ammunition packing box / 弹药包装箱
research.body:
# Ammunition packing box / 弹药包装箱

The game currently uses the Paris city pack's SM_AmmoBox_01a as the finite ammunition supply prop. Its exact historical box pattern, nation, contents and markings have not been identified. War Department TM 9-1900 dated 3 July 1942, printed p34 Figure 11 (PDF p35), provides a period comparison for small-arms ammunition packing boxes: wooden rectangular cases, carrying arrangements and stencilled caliber/content labels. The crop shows these exterior examples only.

当前补给道具采用巴黎城市包的SM_AmmoBox_01a；尚未确认它对应的具体历史箱型、国家、内容物与标记。1942年7月3日《TM 9-1900》印刷页34、图11（PDF页35）可对照轻武器弹药木箱的矩形箱体、提携结构及口径/内容物模板字。配图仅展示箱体外观。

The .30/.50 labels in the illustration identify those illustrated containers, not the contents of the game prop or a match to the player's rifle. Do not label a generic vendor mesh as a verified M1917/M1 box without a matching object record. The game supply remains a finite interaction with existing inventory conservation; it does not automatically contain medicine, refill on saving or establish historical resupply rates.

图中.30/.50字样只说明图示包装，不能当作游戏箱内实际弹药或玩家步枪适配证明。没有匹配证据，不把通用供应商网格标为已核实的M1917/M1箱。游戏仍采用有限库存与原弹药守恒规则；不自动提供药品，不因存档补满。

Primary source scan: https://stephentaylorhistorian.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/tm-9-1900-ammunition-general-1942.pdf#page=35

{"register": "historicalreference/equipment1944/ammunition_box.md", "key": "document", "scope": "equipment", "kind": "note", "title": "ammunition packing box / 弹药包装箱", "body": "# ammunition packing box / 弹药包装箱

the game currently uses the paris city pack's sm_ammobox_01a as the finite ammunition supply prop. its exact historical box pattern, nation, contents and markings have not been identified. war department tm 9-1900 dated 3 july 1942, printed p34 figure 11 (pdf p35), provides a period comparison for small-arms ammunition packing boxes: wooden rectangular cases, carrying arrangements and stencilled caliber/content labels. the crop shows these exterior examples only.

当前补给道具采用巴黎城市包的sm_ammobox_01a；尚未确认它对应的具体历史箱型、国家、内容物与标记。1942年7月3日《tm 9-1900》印刷页34、图11（pdf页35）可对照轻武器弹药木箱的矩形箱体、提携结构及口径/内容物模板字。配图仅展示箱体外观。

the .30/.50 labels in the illustration identify those illustrated containers, not the contents of the game prop or a match to the player's rifle. do not label a generic vendor mesh as a verified m1917/m1 box without a matching object record. the game supply remains a finite interaction with existing inventory conservation; it does not automatically contain medicine, refill on saving or establish historical resupply rates.

图中.30/.50字样只说明图示包装，不能当作游戏箱内实际弹药或玩家步枪适配证明。没有匹配证据，不把通用供应商网格标为已核实的m1917/m1箱。游戏仍采用有限库存与原弹药守恒规则；不自动提供药品，不因存档补满。
